Red-eared sliders are named for the red stripe behind each eye, and for the way they slide off rocks and logs into the water when startled.
The red-eared slider's scientific name is Trachemys scripta elegans, a subspecies of the pond slider.
Red-eared sliders are native to the south-central United States, around the Mississippi River valley, and to northeastern Mexico.
Adult female sliders are noticeably larger than males and can reach about 12 inches (30 cm) in shell length.
Male sliders have very long front claws, which they flutter in front of a female's face during courtship.
Turtles are ectotherms: they rely on outside heat to warm up, which is why sliders spend hours basking.
Basking under UVB light lets sliders make vitamin D3, which they need to absorb calcium for healthy shells and bones.
With good care, red-eared sliders commonly live 20 to 30 years, and some live even longer.
Female sliders can lay eggs even without a male. The eggs are infertile, but she still needs a safe place to dig and lay them.
A slider hatchling's sex depends on how warm its nest is: warmer eggs tend to become females and cooler eggs males.
Young sliders eat mostly insects and other small animals, and they eat more plants as they grow older.
Sliders usually eat in the water, and they generally need water to swallow their food comfortably.
Released pet sliders have spread around the world, and the species is listed among the world's 100 worst invasive species.
Turtles have been around for more than 200 million years, since before the earliest dinosaurs grew large.
A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, built from fused ribs and backbone, so a turtle can never leave its shell.
The top of a turtle's shell is the carapace and the bottom is the plastron. Both are covered in keratin plates called scutes.
Sliders shed the outer layer of their scutes from time to time as they grow, a bit like a snake sheds its skin.
Turtles have no teeth. They bite and tear food with a sharp, keratin-covered beak.
In cold winters, wild sliders brumate: they become sluggish and rest at the bottom of ponds, their metabolism slowed right down.
Since 1975 it has been illegal in the US to sell turtles with shells under 4 inches as pets, because they can spread Salmonella. Wash your hands after handling.
